subject: Clarify SKU bucketing & revenue split for Marketplace private offer
messages:
From: Samantha Ruiz <samantha@dataflux.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer structure question — SKU buckets and channel split

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — we had a good internal sync and are close to pushing a PO to AWS Marketplace via a private offer. Before we commit, procurement needs clarity on two items:

1) SKU bucketing: our finance team wants to confirm how Redwood maps usage to marketplace SKUs. We run a mix of short-lived interactive sessions and periodic batch embedding jobs; will those map to a single SKU or be split across separate SKUs (and pricing tiers)?

2) Outbound revenue allocation / channel margin: DataFlux needs to understand the pass-through calculation used for reseller margin on private offers (how list price -> net revenue is attributed to Redwood vs partner). They need this for rev recognition and to forecast commissions.

Can you send the SKU mapping and a one-page note on channel margin calculations? If possible, small example numbers would be hugely helpful (e.g., $ list price -> marketplace fee -> reseller margin -> net revenue).

Attached is our procurement template — they asked for a sample PO line breakout to sign off.

Best,
Samantha
Procurement Lead, DataFlux
attachments: procurement_template.xlsx
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ruiz <samantha@dataflux.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer structure question — SKU buckets and channel split

Samantha — thanks for the clear ask. Looping Ben (pricing) and Lauren (marketplace ops) to confirm specifics.

Quick summary while they pull details:
- We generally map by product capability + billing unit. Interactive tokens (short sessions) and batch embeddings are separate billing units and therefore can be surfaced as separate SKUs if you want separate line items on the PO.
- For private offers we provide a SKU mapping spreadsheet (attached) that shows common mappings. If you need a custom SKU split for contract purposes we can request custom SKUs on the private offer flow.
- Channel margin: the marketplace (AWS) deducts their transaction fees from list price first; any negotiated reseller margin/pass-through is handled via the private offer pricing delta. Net revenue to Redwood is calculated after marketplace fees and any agreed reseller rebate/commission. Ben and Lauren — can you add a short worked example and confirm whether DataFlux should expect an itemized pass-through on the PO or a single net line?

Attaching: Redwood_SKU_mapping.xlsx and Draft_PO_terms.pdf (draft for internal ops).

- Markus
VP, Partnerships — Redwood Inference

Markus / Lauren — below are the concrete examples I promised. Keeping it intentionally simple so DataFlux can drop numbers into their model. Feel free to paste this back to Samantha.

Example A — Two SKU lines (Interactive + Embeddings)
- List price interactive SKU: $0.020 / 1k tokens
- List price embeddings SKU: $0.004 / 1k embedding units
- Private offer negotiated discount: 20% off list for both SKUs
- AWS transaction fee (example): 5% of list price (this is illustrative; AWS fee schedule applies)

Calculation (interactive SKU, per 1k tokens):
- List price: $0.020.
- AWS fee: 5% of $0.020 = $0.001 -> remaining $0.019
- Private offer discount (20% off list) is applied to buyer price; Marketplace may show the discounted buyer-facing price. Redwood's net revenue = remaining after AWS fee and any reseller commission. If DataFlux negotiating a reseller margin of 10% on the buyer price, that's $0.002 on $0.020, leaving Redwood with ~$0.017 (approx).

Example B — Single aggregated SKU (if DataFlux prefers one PO line)
- You can request a single custom SKU tied to a pricing profile that abstracts both billing units (we then reconcile usage internally). This simplifies the PO but requires clear definitions in the PO terms for how usage is measured. Revenue recognition: marketplace fees are still taken, and any reseller commission is defined in the private offer terms.

Operational notes:
- If you want itemized pass-through on the PO (AWS shows separate lines for fees/commissions), we need early notice so Marketplace ops can enable item-level breakout in the offer. Otherwise the private offer will present a single buyer-facing discounted line and Redwood will handle internal allocation.
- Draft_PO_terms.pdf (attached by Markus) includes suggested language for listing both SKUs and a clause on reseller commission flow.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call with Samantha and procurement to walk through the numbers.

—Ben
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private offer structure question — SKU buckets and channel split

Hi Markus and Samantha,

Thanks for the details — AWS Marketplace here. A few clarifications for the private offer setup:

1) SKU mapping: we can support multiple SKUs on the private offer; each SKU will appear as a separate line item on the buyer invoice. If you want a single aggregated SKU, we require a custom listing change request (timeline ~10 business days).

2) Fees and passthrough: Marketplace transactional fees are assessed against the buyer-facing price. Private offer discounts apply to the buyer-facing price before fees are calculated. Reseller commissions can be provided as a rebate/back-end settlement but are not deducted from the AWS fee calculation. If DataFlux requires itemized reseller pass-through visible on the buyer invoice, confirm in writing and we will request item-level breakout.

3) Timeline: if you want separate SKUs and an itemized pass-through on the PO, please confirm by end of day Friday May 28. Otherwise we will proceed with a single discounted SKU and standard invoice format.

If helpful, I can join the call with Markus and DataFlux procurement — let me know availability.

Regards,

aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com
